Here are the main South Korea stories from early-to-mid October 2026, based on the search results. Most are from the first half of the month, so check outlets directly for later developments.

**Security and North Korea**
- A landmine blast in the DMZ injured South Korean soldiers, and Seoul has demanded an apology while Pyongyang denies planting the mines. A landmine explosion which injured three South Korean soldiers in the Korean Demilitarized Zone last week. S Korea demands apology over DMZ blasts as N Korea denies planting mines.
- Unification Minister Chung Dong-young has urged that Seoul avoid hostility toward Pyongyang and move toward inter-Korean dialogue. He also proposed a trilateral discussion on the exact military demarcation line. Chung said on October 2 that Seoul must not show hostility toward Pyongyang and should use this opportunity to transition to inter-Korean dialogue. Chung proposed a trilateral discussion to demarcate the exact MDL line among Seoul, Pyongyang, and the UNC.
- North Korea has fired ballistic missiles toward the sea. One of the missiles launched from the Pyongyang area flew more than 900km, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. Separately, North Korea says it tested new torpedo with AI tech, reported on October 17.
- An AEI–ISW analysis reports that South Korea's NIS reported that North Korea recently transferred ballistic missiles to Russia for the first time in approximately one year.

**Politics and government**
- During a National Assembly audit, Chief Justice Cho attended this morning's audit, read only the pre-prepared opening remarks as is customary, and refused to take the witness oath. The audit begins today for a run of about a month.
- A Feature piece examines South Korea's Cabinet vetting crises expose decades of presidential resets, covering nomination disputes and the latest reshuffle.

**Economy and finance**
- Markets have been volatile. One analysis describes a five-day KOSPI sell-off that raises questions about whether semiconductor profits will last.
- The won faces its own pressure: With WGBI entry ending in November, pension fund swaps and Washington's investment demands loom over currency policy.
- On trade and investment, Trump unveiled a $200bn South Korean investment package in US projects, and South Korea plans to build 8 nuclear power plants in US, invest $120bn. Seoul says it will only invest in commercially viable projects.

**Security and society**
- In response to recent consecutive hacking incidents in the financial sector, Prime Minister Han Sung-sook has ordered a complete overhaul of security systems.
- In Incheon, the Justice Ministry has apologised after the Incheon suspect met his probation officer hours before the shopping centre rampage. Eight people were injured.

**Space**
- The Nuri rocket was scheduled for its fifth flight, carrying 15 satellites, was moved to the launch pad, with the launch reported as a day away on October 6. I could not confirm the outcome from these results.

**Other**
- Culture: several Korean dramas are airing or premiering this month, including Dive into You | Channel A | September 26 | November 1 | Ongoing and Love in Disguise | tvN | October 18 | November 24 | Awaiting release.

Note that some results carry inconsistent "age" timestamps, so I relied on the dates in the article text.

2026년 10월 중순 기준으로 검색된 한국 주요 이슈는 아래와 같습니다. 검색 결과가 일별 기사 목록과 주간 정리 위주라서, 월 전체를 포괄한 요약은 아닙니다.

**1. 증시 급락과 반도체·AI 불안**
- 주간 정리에 따르면 13일 코스피는 5.5% 급락하며 장중 6,000선이 무너졌다.
- 이틀 뒤인 15일에는 반도체주를 중심으로 매도세가 확산하면서 시장 전체 거래를 일시 중단하는 서킷브레이커가 발동됐다.
- 반면 한 신용평가사는 반도체·AI 호황이 한국 성장 둔화 우려를 상쇄한다고 봤고, 이형일 부총리는 반도체 호황이 내년까지 이어진다고 말했습니다(이형일 부총리 "반도체 호황 내년까지…수요가 공급 웃돌아").

**2. 중동 전쟁과 한국의 역할**
- 국제사회에서는 중동 전쟁을 둘러싼 한국의 군사적 역할이 다시 논쟁의 대상이 됐다.
- 국제유가는 미·이란 협상 교착 속에 반등해 WTI 90달러대 마감했다는 보도도 있습니다.

**3. 한반도 정세**
- 남북 사이의 군사적 긴장이 계속되는 가운데, 북한과 중국 사이에서는 경제적 연결이 더욱 구체화되고 있음을 보여줬다.
- 압록강에서는 사람과 물자가 오갈 수 있는 통로가 실제로 열렸다는 보도가 나왔습니다(사람과 물자가 이동할 수 있는 통로가 실제로 열린 것이다.).

**4. 사회 안전 사건**
- 인천의 한 복합상가에서는 전자발찌를 찬 남성이 흉기를 휘둘러 여러 시민이 다쳤습니다(출처: 데일리25 주간 정리).

**5. 제도 변화**
- 개정 형사소송법이 10월 2일부터 시행됐습니다(개정 형소법 10월 2일 시행…전북경찰청, 수사인력 52명 보강).
- 인천에서도 수사 체계가 바뀌어 검찰청이 사라지고 경찰의 책임이 커진다는 보도가 있었습니다.

**6. 부동산·경제 전망**
- 4분기 부동산 시장을 두고 "비거주 1주택 세 부담 강화 부적절"…전문가들 "거래 위축 우려" 등 전망 기사가 나왔습니다.
- 원·달러 환율 상승과 미국 30년 금리 5.6% 돌파 소식도 있었습니다(이투데이 1일자 헤드라인).

**7. 스포츠**
- 프로야구 KIA는 준플레이오프 1차전에서 승리했습니다(BIG KINDS 헤드라인).
- 전국체전에서는 역도 손현호 선수가 3관왕을 차지했습니다.

정확한 날짜별 흐름이나 세부 내용은 연합뉴스, 조선일보, 한국경제 등 주요 언론의 10월 기사 아카이브나 네이버 뉴스 '월별 주요 뉴스' 페이지에서 한 번 더 확인하시는 것을 권합니다.

Links: [{"title":"South Korea demands North apologize for DMZ mine blasts","url":"https://tribune.net.ph/2026/09/30/south-korea-demands-north-apologize-for-dmz-mine-blasts"},{"title":"North Korea denies it apologized over land mine blast that maimed 2 South Koreans","url":"https://www.foxnews.com/world/north-korea-denies-it-apologized-over-land-mine-blast-that-maimed-2-south-koreans.amp"},{"title":"North Korea denies it apologized over land mine blast _ despite South Korean claims","url":"https://www.foxnews.com/world/north-korea-denies-it-apologized-over-land-mine-blast-_-despite-south-korean-claims.amp"},{"title":"South Korea considers steps to force North Korea apology for DMZ mine blast","url":"https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/6/south-korea-considers-steps-to-force-north-korea-apology-for-dmz-mine-blast"},{"title":"Exclusive news and data that keep market professionals aheadWednesday, September 30, 2026","url":"https://www.uniindia.com/world/defence-dmz-south-korea-north-korea/198297"},{"title":"Print Print    Close Close","url":"https://www.foxnews.com/world/north-korea-denies-it-apologized-over-land-mine-blast-that-maimed-2-south-koreans.print"},{"title":"south korea considers steps to force north korea apology for dmz mine blast","url":"https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/10/6/south-korea-considers-steps-to-force-north-korea-apology-for-dmz-mine-blast"},{"title":"Audio By Carbonatix","url":"https://myjoyonline.com/south-korea-demands-apology-from-pyongyang-for-landmine-blasts-that-injured-three/"},{"title":"S. Korean military launches operation to remove NK mines at recent DMZ blast site","url":"https://koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/defense/20261005/s-korean-military-launches-operation-to-remove-nk-mines-at-recent-dmz-blast-site"},{"title":"North's Kim Yo-jong rejects Seoul's demand for apology over DMZ mine blast","url":"https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/norths-kim-yojong-rejects-seouls-demand-for-apology-over-dmz-mine-blast/12903096"}]

The current dispute stems from a September 21, 2026 blast in the DMZ. Results also included a 2015 incident with a similar pattern, which I've noted separately below.

**The 2026 incident**
- Three South Korean officers were hurt in the blast, and one lost a foot. The explosion happened inside the DMZ, the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice. One lost his foot.
- Seoul's military has called it a violation of the armistice. Kang Hyun-woo of the Joint Chiefs of Staff said the injuries came from North Korean landmines, and he urged an apology and responsible measures.
- A joint South Korean-UN investigation reached a similar conclusion. It found two landmines that exploded last month in the DMZ were planted by North Korean forces about a year ago. The US-led UN Command also confirmed the mine placement violated the 1953 agreement.

**North Korea's response**
- Pyongyang rejects responsibility. Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, called Seoul's claims "groundless" and a "farce" to escalate tensions on the peninsula, and she accused Seoul of "cooking up" the claims.
- She also dismissed the apology demand. Her reported remarks included "What pathetic people they are," Kim said. She added that "We will not allow even the slightest space or room to be entangled or to deal with South Korea in any form."
- North Korea has also warned of retaliation. It accused South Korea of fabricating the findings and warned of "immediate and merciless" retaliation if its troops are fired upon.

**Seoul's next steps**
- Defence Ministry spokeswoman Chung Bin-na said "We are not ruling out any options or prejudging anything" when asked about additional measures to force an apology.
- Seoul has also begun clearing operations. It has discovered two additional land mines at and near the blast site. It pledged to continue with clearing operations in the area if Pyongyang fails to remove the remaining explosives.

**Note on the 2015 incident**
Some results described a 2015 DMZ mine blast that maimed two South Korean soldiers. In that case, Pyongyang expressed "regret," which Seoul treated as an apology, and North Korea later denied that it was one. That episode is separate from the September 2026 blast.

The current dispute stems from a September 21, 2026 blast in the DMZ. Results also included a 2015 incident with a similar pattern, which I've noted separately below.

**The 2026 incident**
- Three South Korean officers were hurt in the blast, and one lost a foot. The explosion happened inside the DMZ, the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice. One lost his foot.
- Seoul's military has called it a violation of the armistice. Kang Hyun-woo of the Joint Chiefs of Staff said the injuries came from North Korean landmines, and he urged an apology and responsible measures.
- A joint South Korean-UN investigation reached a similar conclusion. It found two landmines that exploded last month in the DMZ were planted by North Korean forces about a year ago. The US-led UN Command also confirmed the mine placement violated the 1953 agreement.

**North Korea's response**
- Pyongyang rejects responsibility. Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, called Seoul's claims "groundless" and a "farce" to escalate tensions on the peninsula, and she accused Seoul of "cooking up" the claims.
- She also dismissed the apology demand. Her reported remarks included "What pathetic people they are," Kim said. She added that "We will not allow even the slightest space or room to be entangled or to deal with South Korea in any form."
- North Korea has also warned of retaliation. It accused South Korea of fabricating the findings and warned of "immediate and merciless" retaliation if its troops are fired upon.

**Seoul's next steps**
- Defence Ministry spokeswoman Chung Bin-na said "We are not ruling out any options or prejudging anything" when asked about additional measures to force an apology.
- Seoul has also begun clearing operations. It has discovered two additional land mines at and near the blast site. It pledged to continue with clearing operations in the area if Pyongyang fails to remove the remaining explosives.

**Note on the 2015 incident**
Some results described a 2015 DMZ mine blast that maimed two South Korean soldiers. In that case, Pyongyang expressed "regret," which Seoul treated as an apology, and North Korea later denied that it was one. That episode is separate from the September 2026 blast.

The attack took place on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, in Namdong-gu, Incheon. The Justice Ministry has apologised and promised a review of the suspect's supervision and of electronic monitoring procedures.

**The attack:** Reports describe a 59-year-old man wearing an ankle monitor who injured eight people at a commercial complex in Guwol-dong. He moved from the second basement to the second floor, riding escalators and swinging a knife at passers-by. Bystanders stopped him. Customers stacked chairs at the escalator exit to trap him near the third floor, then pinned him down and took the knife until police arrived. One woman in her 20s underwent surgery after arriving in cardiac arrest. A later report put the injured count at 10, so the figures vary by source. Three criminal profilers were helping investigators establish the motive.

**Supervision history:** The suspect had served a four-year sentence for attempted murder in 2015. After his release in 2019, he was ordered to wear an electronic ankle monitor for 10 years, until February 2029. He had committed no repeat offences while under supervision, the Justice Ministry said. Still, he had previously been punished for breaching restrictions on leaving his home while wearing the device. He had also been booked last month on suspicion of carrying a weapon after a protest incident outside a hospital.

**Probation contact that day:** Ministry figures say he attended a counselling session from 10 to 11 a.m. and then met his probation officer from 11:20 to 11:55 a.m. The officer then had lunch with him until 12.30pm. Authorities detected no attempts to destroy his monitoring device.

**The apology and review:** In a statement, the ministry said "We sincerely apologise over the great public concern caused by the knife attack by an individual under electronic monitoring," adding that it would review both the supervision of the suspect and broader electronic monitoring procedures. It described the probe as covering the circumstances of the incident and the entire electronic monitoring and supervision process. President Lee Jae Myung visited the Incheon Metropolitan Police Agency on Tuesday evening to receive a briefing from senior officers. Police were also told to strengthen preventive measures in crowded public places by deploying sufficient officers.

**Open questions:** Critics say the case shows whether South Korea's system can adequately supervise those deemed high-risk and prevent attacks before they happen. The suspect told investigators he had become frustrated over what he perceived as mistreatment at a hospital.

North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles on Monday, October 12, 2026, and South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said at least one of them flew more than 900 km.

- **Launch details:** The missiles were fired at around 9:20am local time (0020 GMT) from near Pyongyang, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. At least one missile flew more than 900 kilometers.

- **Earlier launch:** The previous launch, on October 3, came from the Wonsan area. The missile flew more than 700 km before falling into the sea, the JCS said. Do not confuse the two: the 900 km figure applies to the October 12 launch.

These are the three biggest South Korea stories from October 11–18, 2026, as I'd rank them:

1. **The KOSPI crashed:** On October 13 the index fell as much as 6% during the day and below 6,000, closing 5.46% lower at 6,035.35 (about an 8% drop over two days) as foreign investors sold heavily and chip stocks like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunged. [Newspim](https://www.newspim.com/news/view/20261013000430)

2. **A stabbing in an Incheon shopping complex:** On October 13 a 59-year-old man wearing an electronic ankle monitor stabbed at least eight people, and the Justice Ministry apologized after it emerged he had met his probation officer only hours before the attack. [SCMP](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3370755/south-korea-shopping-centre-stabbing-leaves-8-injured)

3. **North Korea fired ballistic missiles:** On October 12 North Korea launched several ballistic missiles from near Pyongyang, one of which flew more than 900 km, adding to tensions that were already high after last month's landmine blast in the DMZ. [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/defense/20261013/us-pacific-command-says-n-korea-fired-2-ballistic-missiles-reaffirms-defense-commitment)

A weekly roundup also reported a second sell-off on October 15 that triggered a circuit breaker (a market-wide trading halt), but I couldn't confirm it from a separate source. The ranking is my own judgment.
